title: Why Better Models Can Create Riskier Systems: Evidence from LLM Agents in Financial Markets
abstract: arXiv:2609.04373v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are being deployed at scale in consequential real-world systems, from financial markets to content moderation to hiring. We show that improving individual model capability can degrade rather than improve system-level outcomes. We hypothesize that shared training and architectures can lead more capable LLMs to behave more similarly, creating correlated actions that do not diversify away. We develop a general framework showing how this correlation creates a non-diversifiable risk floor and test its predictions in financial markets using an agent-based simulation with LLM traders of varying general-purpose capability. translated_title: 为什么更好的模型可能创造更危险的系统：来自金融市场中LLM智能体的证据
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLM）正被大规模部署在关乎重大的现实世界系统中，从金融市场到内容审核再到招聘。我们表明，提升单个模型的能力可能会降低而非改善系统层面的结果。我们假设共享的训练数据和架构会使能力更强的LLM表现得更相似，从而产生无法通过分散化消除的相关性行动。我们开发了一个通用框架，展示这种相关性如何形成一个不可分散的风险下限，并在金融市场中通过一个包含不同通用能力LLM交易者的基于智能体的模拟来检验其预测。我们发现：（1）前沿LLM表现出显著的相关性行为，且这种行为随能力的增强而增加；（2）当它们的共享推理准确时，增加智能体参与度可以降低市场层面的风险；（3）当智能体处于共同的错误信息环境中时，同样的相关性行为……
tldr: 提升单个LLM的能力反而可能使系统更危险——由于共享训练导致模型行为高度相关，形成无法分散的系统性风险下限。
en_tdlr: Improving individual LLM capability can worsen system-level outcomes, because shared training makes models behave more similarly, creating correlated actions and a non-diversifiable risk floor.
